title: AI that runs the business of the firm
summary: Celeste is Intapp's expert AI coworker for the business of your firm. It screens deals, clears conflicts, and runs playbooks — grounded in your data.
body_text: Walk into any law firm, private equity firm, investment bank, or accounting firm today and nearly every desk is using AI. Your professionals draft, build models, and review documents faster than they did a year ago. That was the right first move, and the gains are real. But here’s the question we keep hearing from firm leaders: Our people are more productive, so why isn’t the firm growing faster? The answer: Because AI built for the practice accelerates individuals. Meanwhile, the work that runs the firm itself — origination, screening, intake, conflicts, lateral hiring — still happens the way it always has: by hand, under deadline, by your most experienced people. And because their hours are finite, the firm rations that work — resulting in deals never screened, laterals never vetted, pitches never made. This is what Firm AI changes — and it changes more than speed. A conflicts team that clears 20 matters a month can clear 200. A fund that screens 300 deals a year can screen 3,000, and can pursue entire categories of opportunity it used to filter out for practical reasons. More than saved time, this is a new operating model for the firm. It’s why we built Intapp Celeste, now generally available . Meet Celeste Celeste is an expert AI coworker for the business of your firm. Give Celeste a goal, and it plans the steps, executes them across your firm’s systems, and brings finished work back for a professional’s judgment. It doesn’t wait to be asked — it just runs your pipeline brief every Monday morning, or starts a conflicts check the moment a new engagement lands. Plenty of tools can answer a question about your work. Four things make Celeste a strategic coworker instead. Celeste knows your firm Every firm now has access to the same AI models, trained on the same public internet. What sets your firm apart is exactly what those models don’t know: your clients, your deals, your relationships, and the judgment behind every decision your firm has made. An AI without that context gives every firm the same answer. Celeste greets each professional with work in progress, playbooks ready to run, and a place to hand off the next job. Celeste is grounded in all of it. Natively integrated with your systems of record, Celeste inherits everything you’ve spent years configuring: your operating model, your terminology, your fields and data structures, your permissions. Celeste knows what “pipeline” and “coverage” mean at your private equity firm, and what “matter” and “key client” mean at your law firm, the way you define them. Context engine. A firm profile, connector onboarding, and domain model teach Celeste your data, your terms, and your relationships, so it reasons in your firm’s language. Native Intapp integration. Celeste connects across Intapp DealCloud, your compliance systems, and Intapp Time to draw on deal and matter history, relationships, and client activity. Memory. Celeste remembers your patterns, decisions, and preferences, and grounds its answers in the documents you choose. Celeste gets the work done An assistant answers your questions and waits for the next one — but those answers aren’t finished deliverables. And besides, the work that runs a firm doesn’t arrive in the form of questions; it arrives as jobs — CIMs to screen, matters to open, Monday meetings to prep for. But Celeste delivers finished products: IC summaries drafted, records updated, briefs sent to your inbox — with your sign-off required at the points that carry risk. And because Celeste works before you ask, and at whatever volume the work demands, it takes on jobs no firm could staff before: screening every inbound deal against your mandate, or monitoring every lateral hire from sourcing through integration. Proactive agents. Celeste works in the background on schedules and events, then surfaces a curated agenda of finished work that’s ready for review. Document intelligence. Celeste produces Word, PowerPoint, and Excel files in your firm’s templates and branding, and edits existing documents with tracked changes. Read-and-write actions. Celeste automates follow-ups, task sequencing, and record updates across Intapp and connected systems, keeping your teams focused on client work. Celeste works your firm’s way Getting the work done is half the job. Doing it your way is the other half: the criteria you screen against, the order you run a conflicts check in, the way a pitch reads when it comes from your firm. Those methods are what separate you from the firm across the street — and until now they lived only in the heads of the people who use them. Celeste encodes your methods as playbooks: multi-step agentic workflows that carry out your firm’s procedures from the first step to the finished output, so the work comes back the way your firm would have done it. Celeste ships with a library of playbooks curated by Intapp industry experts and shaped by our work with more than 1,000 firms — ready to run out of the box or tailor to how your firm operates. Playbook library. Access pre-built playbooks across deal origination, compliance, lateral hiring, business development, and more. No-code builder. Create your own playbooks, agents, and skills in plain language, then run them right from chat. Automations. Set playbooks to run on your schedule or start automatically when something changes in your systems, and get notifications in the app or by email. Celeste enforces your guardrails Professional firms operate under obligations most industries don’t: ethical walls, client confidentiality, independence requirements, MNPI. Any AI that touches your firm’s data must honor every one of them the way your people do — or else your general counsel will stop the rollout, and rightly so. Celeste has those guardrails architected into its core, and applies your ethical walls and access policies through a trust and control layer that governs Celeste by the same rules as your people — so restricted information stays that way, no matter what anyone asks. Guardrails. Permissions, ethical walls, and access controls run through one policy layer for trust and controls across human and AI identities, and Celeste acts only on what it’s permitted to use. Human-in-the-loop review. Sensitive tasks require review, approval, or refinement of Celeste’s actions before it executes. Celeste connects across your ecosystem Celeste also works where your work already lives. At launch, it connects natively to Intapp DealCloud, your compliance systems, Intapp Time, Microsoft 365, Snowflake, and the open web, with Model Context Protocol (MCP) partners including Moody’s, FactSet, PitchBook, and MSCI. It also meets your teams inside the AI tools they already use, working in Microsoft Copilot, Claude, and other tools through MCP, A2A, and API. No rip and replace. Get started We were able to build Celeste because of what we spent over 20 years building: the relationship data in DealCloud, the compliance backbone, and the working methods of more than 1,000 firms. Celeste is that foundation, put to work. title: Group classes vs. 1:1 tutoring: which format fits your child?
summary: Small group classes and one-on-one tutoring solve different problems. An honest, research-backed framework for choosing the right format by subject, learner, and budget.
body_text: A quick decision framework When you are unsure, run through these four questions: Is this remediation or enrichment? A specific gap points toward one-on-one. Exploring or deepening an interest points toward a group. How does my child respond to peers? Energized and motivated, lean group. Self-conscious or easily distracted by others, lean one-on-one, at least to start. Does the subject reward discussion? Writing, reading, and the humanities gain from many voices. A single stubborn math concept usually does not. What is the budget and timeline? One-on-one costs more per hour but can work faster on a narrow goal. Groups stretch a budget and suit ongoing, lower-pressure learning. Many families end up using both, and that is often the smartest play: a group class for a subject your child enjoys and wants to go deeper in, plus a few one-on-one sessions to shore up a weak spot before it snowballs. How ESA funds change the math If you have an Education Savings Account, format matters less to your wallet than it used to. Most ESA programs cover both group classes and private tutoring as approved expenses, which means you can match the format to your child's need rather than your budget. That is a genuine shift, and it is worth revisiting a plan you set before your funds arrived. Where Outschool fits One reason we point families toward format first is that Outschool offers both. You can enroll in an ongoing small group class or book one-on-one tutoring with the same vetted teachers, and switch between them as your child's needs change. For a broader look at how platforms stack up, our online tutoring comparison guide breaks down the major options. Two related reads if you are still weighing your approach: our comparison of an online writing tutor versus a writing app , and a quick quiz on whether your child is ready for self-paced classes . Frequently asked questions Is one-on-one tutoring always more effective? For closing a specific, well-defined gap, usually yes. For discussion-based subjects, motivation, and collaborative skills, a group can produce better outcomes and stick better over time. What counts as a "small" group? There is no official number, but the benefits of personalization start to fade quickly above roughly eight to ten kids. Ask about class size before you enroll. Can shy kids do well in group classes? Many do, especially in small, warmly run groups where the teacher draws everyone in. If your child is very anxious about peers, starting one-on-one and transitioning to a group later is a reasonable path. How do I know if it is working? Look for two signals within a few weeks: your child is less resistant to showing up, and they can explain something they could not before. If neither is moving, revisit the format. Start with the problem you are trying to solve, not the format everyone recommends. Match the setup to your child, and stay willing to switch when the need changes. The best format is the one your child will keep showing up for. Sources [1] Bloom, B. S. (1984). The 2 Sigma Problem. title: Braiin and Home Announce Exclusive Strategic Partnership to Pioneer "LiveTech" and Build AI-Native Living Infrastructure Platform
body_text: A category-defining partnership combining AI, payments and embedded distribution NEW YORK, NY AND LONDON, UK / ACCESS Newswire / April 2, 2026 / Braiin Limited (NASDAQ: BRAI ) ( "Braiin" or "the Company") and Home.cc ("Home") today announced an exclusive strategic partnership to build and scale an AI-driven Living Infrastructure platform spanning the global home lifecycle. The platform will launch in the UK, with expansion to follow across the US, ANZ, and Europe. The partnership combines Braiin's AI and unified home wallet with Home's orchestration layer, payment rails, and embedded distribution to create a system operating at the point of transaction, transforming how consumers move, activate, and manage their homes. Together, the companies are introducing "LiveTech," a new category similar to fintech and proptech focused on integrating and monetizing the services that power modern living. Natraj Balasubramanium, CEO of Braiin Limited, commented: "This partnership is not just about scaling a product - it establishes a distribution and monetization layer for our broader AI ecosystem. By embedding at the point of property transaction, we capture high-intent customer flows and convert them into recurring, data-rich relationships, creating a scalable, AI-driven system that transforms how services are delivered and monetized across the home. "Together with Home, we are bringing distribution, payments, and intelligence into a single operating layer, moving from fragmented service delivery to a coordinated, data-driven model that improves conversion, reduces friction, and expands lifetime value, particularly through a platform already deeply embedded in property ecosystems. In the same way that fintech redefined financial services and proptech modernized real estate, we believe LiveTech represents the next evolution - integrating the full lifecycle of living into a unified, intelligent infrastructure. "This materially strengthens our PropTech platform while creating cross-vertical leverage across our AI, CX, and payments infrastructure, reinforcing our view that infrastructure integration is a powerful driver of long-term revenue growth. LiveTech represents the commercialization of that strategy - a structural shift from point solutions to integrated infrastructure, where intelligence, distribution, and monetization converge into a single, unified system." Accelerating Growth Through Infrastructure Integration Having established its core technology, integrations, and partner ecosystem, Connect Simple now transitions from a standalone platform to a scaled infrastructure layer within the LiveTech ecosystem - leveraging embedded distribution, data, and AI to drive customer acquisition, conversion, and recurring revenue. Multiple industry forecasts project that the global PropTech market could exceed US$100 billion by 2030, with the UK market also expected to see strong growth through the end of the decade. With access to millions of movers annually through embedded distribution, the combined platform is positioned to capture a high-intent, high-conversion segment of this market, supporting efficient acquisition and monetization within a large and expanding market. These figures represent only a subset of a broader multi-trillion-dollar global opportunity across housing and living-related spend. The alliance with Home is expected to materially accelerate Connect Simple's revenue growth over the next 18-24 months and further support Braiin's previously disclosed projections for Connect Simple and its broader strategy of scaling platform assets through infrastructure integration and embedded distribution into globally competitive, high-growth platforms. Matt Spence, Founder and CEO of Home, commented: "What makes this partnership powerful is not just the technology - it's where it sits. Home is embedded at the point of transaction across the property ecosystem, at the exact moment when consumers are making decisions that define their living experience. That position gives us a unique ability to turn what has traditionally been a fragmented, one-time interaction into a continuous, monetizable relationship across the entire home lifecycle. "By combining that embedded distribution with Braiin's AI, data, and payments infrastructure, we are not just improving the move-we are building a system that extends far beyond it, one that connects services, simplifies decisions, and continues to create value long after the keys are handed over. LiveTech reflects that evolution: from helping people move, to enabling how they live - through an integrated platform that brings together the full stack of services, intelligence, and infrastructure required to operate the modern home." Importantly, Connect Simple will continue to be led by its original core team, reinforcing Braiin's commitment to founder-led stewardship, operational continuity, and building enduring partnerships as the platform scales. Through integration with Home's embedded distribution layer and Braiin's AI-driven Living Infrastructure platform, Connect Simple gains immediate direct access to high-intent customer flows at the point of move-in, where service activation decisions are made. In addition, Connect Simple leverages Braiin's ProEval Enterprise capabilities to enhance its platform with: Real-time performance scoring and conversion optimisation AI-driven compliance monitoring and audit trails Omnichannel interaction intelligence across voice, chat, and digital workflows Data-driven insights to improve customer experience and operational efficiency These capabilities are designed to accelerate customer acquisition through embedded distribution; conversion rates via AI-driven automation and intelligent workflows; and recurring revenue growth through lifecycle monetisation and recurring services. Embedded Distribution at Scale Through its partnership with the Tenancy Deposit Scheme (TDS), tenant app Tlyfe, and B2B platform FCC Paragon, Home is embedded at the point of transaction across the UK property ecosystem. With integrations including Chestertons and Douglas & Gordon, the platform reaches approximately 4.5 million movers annually and more than 75,000 monthly leads, representing a meaningful share of the UK move-in market at the point of transaction. title: The Importance of Student & Staff Wellbeing: A conversation with Chatham County Schools Superintendent Dr. Anthony Jackson
body_text: SUPERINTENDENT INTERVIEW SERIES Daybreak Health CEO Alex Alvarado talks to Superintendents from across the country to discuss topics and trends affecting their school communities like chronic absenteeism, student mental health, academic outcomes, and more. These Superintendents represent districts from urban to rural, large to small, and range in their minority enrollment and number of students who are economically disadvantaged. Our goal is to capture different voices and perspectives on the challenges facing our schools today. Chatham County Schools Superintendent Dr. Anthony Jackson, a lifelong educator, shares the ethos of the district, exploring themes of culture, fostering excellence, and the importance of student and staff wellbeing. Creating a Culture of Belonging At the heart of Dr. Jackson's leadership philosophy lies a profound commitment to fostering a culture where every individual feels seen, valued, and empowered to thrive. Transparency, open communication, and a shared focus on problem-solving form the bedrock of this culture. Dr. Jackson's background as a music teacher imbued in him the virtues of collaboration, improvisation, and harmony, which he seamlessly translates into his role as superintendent: “The lessons I learned in music are truly the lessons that I bring to the leadership table,” says Dr. Jackson. “Collaboration, cooperation, improvisation, structure, all of those things matter as a leader, but they're essential as a musician. To read music, you learn very quickly that your eyes have to see things that your fingers or your instrument don’t quite yet react to. So that's kind of a whole notion of visionary leadership.” Just as a skilled musician anticipates the notes ahead, Dr. Jackson encourages his team to envision future challenges and proactively navigate them with resilience and creativity. He shared, “Sometimes as a leader you have to be able to see things that aren't quite there yet.” Through nurturing authentic relationships and prioritizing the needs of students, Chatham County Schools cultivates a community where everyone feels a sense of belonging and purpose. Prioritizing Educator & Staff Wellbeing Just as the wellbeing of students is a priority, Dr. Jackson emphasizes the significance of supporting the holistic wellness of educators and staff as well. “Probably the biggest challenge that I'm seeing right now is that we have to be as intentional with adult wellbeing as we are with student wellbeing,” says Dr. Jackson. “I believe that if we're going to meet the needs of students, the adults have to be healthy and whole. And for them to be healthy and whole, we've got to be very deliberate about providing pathways and opportunities for them to check in and take care of themselves. So that we can, without apology, ask them to take care of our kids.” Acknowledging the immense pressures and challenges faced by adults in the educational ecosystem, the district implements initiatives to promote self-care and resilience. “We go overboard to ensure we are consistently communicating to our staff about the importance of their mental health and wellbeing to try to destigmatize it.” By normalizing discussions around mental health and providing resources such as Employee Assistance Programs (EAPs), Chatham County Schools fosters a culture of care and compassion where individuals feel empowered to prioritize their wellbeing without stigma or judgment. “Self-care is not being selfish,” he says. “You really have to do something for yourself every day.” Equitable Mental Health Support for Students The evolving landscape of student mental health demands a multifaceted approach that goes beyond traditional paradigms. Dr. Jackson said, “We can't solve our post-COVID reality with pre-COVID strategy. We have to be so very open to trying new things.” He underscores the importance of recognizing students' cries for help and providing them with safe spaces to express their challenges and aspirations. “I see students who are craving attention––but not just attention. They are craving real relationships where they can honestly build understanding about the pathways that are in front of them.” He added, “We have to be open to hearing them, listening to them, giving them voices, and build space safe places for these kids to ask questions, get answers, and express who they are and what they're thinking. [We want] to give them the ability to work closely with school staff and their families to problem-solve.” “We have behavior specialists and we've invested heavily in our MTSS model here so that we can identify our kids with the greatest need, and get support for them as quickly as we possibly can,” says Dr. Jackson. The partnership with Daybreak exemplifies Chatham County Schools' commitment to addressing mental health needs proactively. By offering innovative solutions such as teletherapy, the district ensures that students receive timely and tailored interventions. Through collaborative efforts with local partners and leveraging technology, Chatham County Schools endeavors to bridge the gap between mental health needs and accessible support services. ‍ The Impact of Daybreak Partnership The collaboration between Chatham County Schools and Daybreak marks a transformative milestone in the district's journey towards holistic student mental health support: “Daybreak helps us triage at the front end. We can help students and families before we get to that critical need where they need face-to-face intervention.” By expanding access to mental health services and leveraging innovative approaches, the partnership empowers students to navigate challenges and thrive academically, emotionally, and socially. “We don't wait for the students to fall apart before we try to support them,” says Dr. Jackson. “That's the biggest lesson. We can't wait for them to fall apart before we start intervening. And so that's why we're really, really thrilled to be working with Daybreak, as well as our local partners, our school social workers and counselors to try to build that safe place for kids.” The district’s creative use of resources is necessary in a time where schools lack the resources to meet every student’s needs: “We find ourselves in a place where we have more need than we have capacity. So in our community––which is a pretty well resourced community––we don't have enough support to meet the needs of our students. So we have to go out and look for innovative ways of being able to get support for our kids.” The Daybreak partnership is a cornerstone of the district's support framework and underscores the district’s unwavering commitment to ensuring that every student receives the resources and care they need to succeed. “Our goal is to try to figure out ways to get more and more [mental health] support into the places where we need them. So we have to be innovative. That's why teletherapy works,” says Dr. Jackson. “It has been a tremendous partnership [with Daybreak] that we hope to leverage in the interest of kids as we move forward. Unapologetically, we care about our kids. And so we're going to do whatever is necessary to ensure that they are healthy and whole.” Chatham County Schools epitomizes the convergence of visionary leadership, compassionate stewardship, and a relentless pursuit of excellence. Dr. Jackson is steadfast in his dedication to nurturing a culture of empathy, belonging, and wellbeing to meet the educational and emotional goals of this generation. ‍

title: Programmatic Ad Targeting: Key Types and How They Improve Audience Reach
summary: What are the programmatic targeting types? Compare audience, contextual, behavioral, geo, retargeting and cross-device, and when to use each.
body_text: Programmatic Ad Targeting: Key Types and How They Improve Audience Reach July 14, 2026 in Blog Key Findings: Effective methods of programmatic ad targeting include: audience targeting, contextual targeting, behavioral targeting, geotargeting, cross-device targeting and retargeting. By employing programmatic ad targeting, marketers can be sure their budgets are going toward ads delivered only to relevant audiences. With Viant, marketers can create customized audience segments for targeting by leveraging people-based data, not anonymous cookies. Choosing the right programmatic targeting type, and layering several together, helps marketers balance reach and precision across every stage of the funnel. As third-party cookies decline, first-party and people-based data have become the durable foundation for effective, privacy-safe audience targeting. What Is Programmatic Ad Targeting? Programmatic ad targeting is the automated, data-driven process of buying and placing digital advertisements to reach specific, highly defined target audiences in real time. Rather than relying on manual placement or static negotiations, programmatic targeting leverages automated technology and data signals to instantly evaluate and serve ads to the most relevant users across channels. Programmatic ad targeting offers a simple solution: It helps brands reach the right people with the right content. By tapping into consumers’ locations, behaviors and more, ads can reach ideal audiences for maximum engagement. For example, let’s say your brand sells skincare products that you’re marketing to women in their 20s and 30s. With programmatic ad targeting, you’re able to create a segment of relevant consumers and then funnel your messaging to this specific group and to individuals within that group who are more likely to be in need of your offerings. How Programmatic Targeting Works Translating a high-level audience strategy into real-world results requires a technical engine that operates in milliseconds. At the center of programmatic targeting is the Demand-Side Platform (DSP), an automated software tool that evaluates billions of ad impression opportunities in real time to match advertisers with their ideal consumers. To execute precise targeting, DSPs ingest, process, and synthesize three primary tiers of data: First-party data: Direct, proprietary consumer insights collected by the advertiser, including CRM records, purchase histories, and website interactions. Second-party data: Another organization’s first-party data shared through direct strategic partnerships, such as retail media networks or publisher insights. Third-party data: Aggregated behavioral, intent, and demographic information acquired from external data providers to broaden campaign reach. Historically, DSPs relied heavily on third-party cookies and mobile ad IDs to connect these data tiers across browsers and devices. But as browser privacy changes and data regulations accelerate the shift to cookieless, legacy tracking signals are disappearing. Marketers relying on outdated tracking face degraded targeting accuracy, limited reach, and fragmented measurement. To solve this challenge, modern programmatic strategies require persistent, privacy-first identity resolution. Solutions like the Viant Household ID™ offer a key differentiator by anchoring targeting data to confirmed, real-world physical addresses rather than transient digital cookies. By mapping all connected devices within a residence to a single physical household, marketers can maintain high-precision audience targeting, strict frequency control, and closed-loop attribution in a cookieless landscape. Like the example above, programmatic ad targeting types each serve their own purpose. Here are six effective methods for targeting and how they can be used to help create a successful ad campaign. Types Of Programmatic Targeting For Advertising Targeting Type What It Uses Best For Primary Data Source Cookieless Ready? Audience Targeting Demographics, interests, and modeled segments such as age, income, and lifestyle Reaching a defined customer profile at scale across the funnel First-party and second-party data, identity graphs Yes, with first-party or people-based identity Contextual Targeting Page content, topic, and sentiment analyzed in real time Privacy-safe prospecting and brand-safe placements without user data Page-level content signals (no personal data) Yes, natively Behavioral Targeting Past actions such as site visits, product views, and purchase history High-intent prospecting and re-engagement of active researchers First-party behavioral data Partial, depends on first-party signals Geotargeting Region, city, or ZIP-level location signals Local campaigns, events, and store or region-specific offers Location and device signals Yes Retargeting Prior engagement with a brand or website Recapturing warm audiences and driving return visits or conversions First-party pixel and CRM data Partial, depends on durable identifiers Cross-Device Targeting Device activity linked to a single person or household Sequencing messaging across CTV, mobile, and desktop Household or person-level identity resolution Yes, with people-based identity Audience Targeting As one of the most common and frequently used ad targeting types, audience targeting lets businesses serve ads to specific populations based on characteristics such as gender, household income, age, interests and more. Basically, the perfect customer. A mix of first-party and third-party data is often combined to generate audience lists that advertisers can then buy and serve ads to. This can be useful for businesses that know what type of customer they want to reach but may not know where to look for them. Learn more about audience segmentation Contextual Targeting Contextual targeting looks at exactly that: the context. By using data to determine what types of content appear on the websites people are viewing, contextual targeting allows for relevant ads to appear alongside related articles, often on editorial publishers’ sites. If you’ve ever read a product review online for, say, headphones, and you’re served an ad for a pair of noise-blocking earbuds while scrolling, that’s likely an example of contextual targeting. Behavioral Targeting Behavioral targeting looks at personal behaviors, such as shopping habits, website interactions and product interests. This programmatic ad targeting type dives deep into the individual consumer to target their unique lifestyle. It takes into account what people do on website pages they visit, or don’t do, such as adding items to a cart, adding items to a cart and then leaving a site without a purchase, making a purchase or sharing a link with others. Rather than just solving whom ads should go to and where, behavioral targeting takes into account why these ads will matter to consumers. Geotargeting A study conducted by The Harris Poll on behalf of The New York Times found that nearly 80% of U.S. adults have location-sharing features activated on their mobile devices. Through geotargeting, a type of location-based targeting, ads can be served to people based on their region or zip code. Marketers often compare geotargeting vs geofencing to determine whether to reach audiences within broader geographic areas or trigger ads based on more precise, real-time location signals. For example, an event planning company putting on a local show would want to use geotargeting to serve ads to nearby individuals who are within reasonable distance to attend and purchase tickets. Retargeting If you’ve ever browsed the web and were served ads for the same product across different websites, you were looking at a form of retargeting. This approach, which leverages data to serve ads to users who have shown an interest in your brand previously, can be an effective strategy for encouraging consumers to revisit your site or re-engage with your brand. Retargeting is a way to rekindle consumers’ interest in your brand and encourage them to make further purchases. Cross-Device Targeting This highly valuable programmatic ad targeting type gives businesses the opportunity to serve targeted ads across numerous digital devices based on device activity and use. According to data from Pew Research Center , 90% of U.S. adults own a smartphone and roughly 80% own a desktop or laptop computer . Cross-device targeting lets brands reach consumers seamlessly from one screen to the next. Therefore, a person served an ad on their laptop can be re-engaged with a tailored follow-up on their mobile phone. How To Choose and Combine Targeting Types The most effective programmatic campaigns rarely rely on a single targeting method in isolation. Instead, the strongest strategies thoughtfully layer multiple targeting types so each approach covers the blind spots of the others. This multi-layered structure naturally follows funnel logic: upper-funnel strategies like contextual and demographic audience targeting generate broad awareness and prospect for net-new buyers, while lower-funnel tactics like behavioral targeting and retargeting focus on converting warm, high-intent prospects. Combining targeting types allows marketers to build highly tailored campaign tactics: Contextual + Behavioral: Reach brand-new prospects consuming relevant content, then re-engage those specific users who demonstrate active purchase intent down the line. Geotargeting + Retargeting: Drive local foot traffic or event attendance in targeted geographic areas, then re-engage nearby consumers who interacted with your initial ads. Audience + Cross-Device: Define a precise, high-value audience segment and deliver a persistent brand story across Connected TV, mobile, and desktop screens. Sustaining campaign efficiency across these combinations requires two critical operational levers: frequency capping and audience exclusions. Setting strict frequency caps prevents ad fatigue, protects user experience, and spreads your media budget across a broader pool of prospects. Meanwhile, applying audience exclusions filters out recent buyers or current customers, ensuring spend remains focused strictly on net-new customer acquisition. Ultimately, programmatic ad targeting is not a set-and-forget discipline. Marketers must treat targeting as an evolving process, using real-time campaign performance data to continuously refine their tactics, balance their audience mix, and maximize overall ROI. Audience targeting reaches people by demographics and interests, contextual places ads based on page content, behavioral uses past actions, geotargeting works by location, retargeting re-engages prior visitors, and cross-device follows a person or household across screens. Most campaigns combine several of these types rather than relying on one, layering signals to balance reach and precision. What is programmatic audience targeting? Expand Programmatic audience targeting is the practice of using automated technology to serve ads to specific groups of people based on shared traits such as demographics, interests, and past behavior. It builds those groups from first-party and modeled data, then activates them in real time across channels through a demand-side platform (DSP). The goal is to reach the people most likely to act while minimizing spend on irrelevant impressions. How does programmatic audience targeting work? Expand It works by matching advertiser-defined audience segments against available ad impressions in real time, evaluating each one in milliseconds before an ad is served. Audience signals like interests, purchase intent, and device activity are layered together, and the DSP bids on impressions that fit the defined criteria. This automated, per-impression decisioning is what separates programmatic from manually placed media buys. What is the difference between audience targeting and contextual targeting? Expand The difference is that audience targeting reaches people based on who they are, while contextual targeting reaches people based on what they are currently reading or watching. Audience targeting relies on data about the user, while contextual targeting relies only on the content of the page, which makes it privacy-safe and effective without cookies. Expand Yes, programmatic advertising targeting remains effective without third-party cookies by shifting to first-party data, contextual signals, and people-based identity resolution. Advertisers who invested early in first-party data have seen minimal disruption from cookie deprecation. What is first-party data and why does it matter for programmatic targeting? Expand First-party data is information a company collects directly from its own audience, such as website activity, purchases, email sign-ups, and CRM records. It matters for programmatic targeting because it is accurate, consent-based, and durable as third-party cookies disappear, making it the most reliable foundation for building and activating audience segments. Brands that invest in collecting and structuring first-party data retain far more targeting precision than those that relied on third-party sources. How does retargeting work in programmatic advertising? Expand Retargeting works by serving ads to people who have already interacted with your brand, such as visiting your site or viewing a product, to bring them back toward a conversion. A pixel or first-party data source adds those users to an audience segment, and the DSP then serves relevant ads to them across other sites and devices. Segmenting by intent stage, such as separating general visitors from cart abandoners, makes retargeting far more effective than treating all past visitors the same. But let's be honest—for many of us, the honeymoon phase is showing some cracks. The introduction of the Daily Pass on beloved completed series, the sometimes frustrating content restrictions, and the sheer volume of comics to sift through can leave you wondering: what else is out there? You're not alone. Across Reddit threads and Discord servers, readers are asking the same question. The good news is that the world of webcomics is bigger than ever. The perfect platform for you is out there, and it all depends on what you're trying to fix. This guide breaks down the best WEBTOON alternatives based on the most common frustrations, giving you a quick solution for your specific comic craving. The Problem: "I'm tired of the Daily Pass and restrictive paywalls." You fell in love with a series, binged 100 chapters for free, and now the completed version is locked behind a system that makes you pay or wait a day for a single chapter. It's one of the community's biggest frustrations. Quick Solution: Tapas Why it works: Tapas is often seen as WEBTOON's closest competitor, and its monetization system can feel more rewarding. Many of its premium series operate on a "Wait Until Free" model, where you can unlock an episode by waiting a few days. Crucially, Tapas also offers numerous ways to earn their premium currency, "Ink," by watching ads, participating in events, and engaging with the community. Community Vibe: As one user on the r/otomeisekai subreddit noted, "Tapas feels more generous with its free ink events. It's known for a strong indie creator scene alongside its licensed Korean manhwa, giving it a diverse, community-driven feel. The Problem: "I want mature, uncensored stories that aren't afraid to get dark or spicy." You're looking for a thriller with real consequences, a horror comic that is genuinely terrifying, or a romance that explores adult themes without fading to black. WEBTOON's content guidelines, while understandable, often mean that creators have to censor their work, leaving readers hungry for more intensity. Quick Solution #1: Lezhin Comics Why it works: Lezhin is the undisputed king of premium, mature content. It's the platform creators go to when their stories are too spicy, gory, or psychologically intense for mainstream apps. It is famous for its incredible library of high-quality Boys' Love (BL), Girls' Love (GL), and adult romance, all completely uncensored. Community Vibe: Lezhin is for serious readers who are willing to pay for premium, uncensored art and storytelling. The general consensus is that while it's expensive (nearly everything is pay-per-chapter), the quality is often unmatched. It's the "HBO" of webcomics. Quick Solution #2: Shortbread Why it works: If Lezhin is the established premium option, Shortbread is the exciting newcomer built for spice and intensity. It's a fantastic middle-ground for readers who want more edge without a strictly 18+ label on everything. body_text: Access to emergency contraception has become easier for women across England following the introduction of a new NHS pharmacy scheme. According to the latest figures, more than 300,000 doses of the morning after pill have been supplied through participating community pharmacies during the first five months of the initiative. The scheme represents a significant step forward in improving access to reproductive healthcare. Women no longer need to arrange a GP appointment or visit a sexual health clinic in many cases, allowing them to receive emergency contraception quickly from trained pharmacists. Since emergency contraception works best when taken as soon as possible after unprotected sex or contraceptive failure, reducing delays can make a meaningful difference. More Than 300,000 Emergency Contraceptive Pills Dispensed New NHS data shows that approximately 305,000 emergency contraceptive pills were provided through pharmacies between October 2025 and March 2026. The figures highlight strong public uptake of the service and demonstrate the growing role that community pharmacies play in delivering essential healthcare. The initiative was designed to remove barriers that previously made accessing emergency contraception more difficult. Many women faced challenges such as securing same-day GP appointments, traveling to specialist clinics, or paying privately for the medication. The expanded pharmacy service helps eliminate many of these obstacles. Healthcare professionals have welcomed the early success of the program, noting that pharmacies are often more convenient, offer longer opening hours, and are available in many local communities. How the NHS Pharmacy Scheme Works Under the NHS scheme, eligible women can visit participating community pharmacies to receive a confidential consultation with a trained pharmacist. Following an assessment, the pharmacist can provide emergency contraception free of charge when appropriate. The consultation includes discussions about: The timing of unprotected sex Current medications Medical history The most suitable emergency contraception option Advice about ongoing contraception Sexual health guidance where appropriate Because pharmacists are highly trained healthcare professionals, they can provide advice quickly while ensuring the medication is supplied safely. Why Quick Access Matters Emergency contraception is most effective when taken as soon as possible after unprotected sexual intercourse or contraceptive failure. While certain emergency contraceptive pills can be effective for several days after intercourse, their effectiveness generally improves the earlier they are taken. Common reasons someone may need emergency contraception include: A condom breaking or slipping off Missing contraceptive pills Forgotten contraception Unprotected sex Concerns that regular contraception may not have worked properly Having pharmacies provide faster access can reduce unnecessary delays, giving women more opportunities to obtain treatment within the recommended timeframe. Community Pharmacies Are Becoming Key Healthcare Providers The success of this initiative also reflects the expanding role of community pharmacies within the NHS. Over recent years, pharmacists have increasingly provided a wider range of healthcare services beyond dispensing prescriptions. Many pharmacies now offer services such as: Blood pressure checks Vaccinations Minor illness consultations Smoking cessation support Contraception services Emergency contraception These expanded responsibilities help reduce pressure on GP surgeries while making healthcare more convenient for patients. Benefits of Pharmacy-Based Emergency Contraception Providing emergency contraception through pharmacies offers several advantages. Faster Access Women can often visit a pharmacy without needing to wait for a GP appointment, making it easier to obtain treatment promptly. Greater Convenience Many pharmacies are open during evenings and weekends, providing additional flexibility for patients who cannot attend daytime appointments. Improved Privacy Consultations take place in private consultation rooms, allowing women to discuss sensitive healthcare matters confidentially. Reduced Healthcare Pressure By allowing pharmacists to deliver this service, GP practices and sexual health clinics can focus on patients requiring more complex medical care. Importance of Ongoing Contraception Healthcare professionals emphasize that emergency contraception should not replace regular contraception. Instead, it provides a backup option when regular contraception has failed or was not used. During pharmacy consultations, pharmacists may discuss longer-term contraceptive choices and recommend speaking with a GP or sexual health provider about options that best suit individual needs. Available contraceptive methods include oral contraceptive pills, implants, intrauterine devices (IUDs), injections, patches, and condoms. Public Health Impact Improving access to emergency contraception can contribute to broader public health goals by helping reduce unintended pregnancies and ensuring women receive timely reproductive healthcare. Removing financial barriers is also important. Previously, some women purchased emergency contraception privately when unable to access NHS services quickly. The nationwide pharmacy scheme offers an accessible alternative that is available without direct cost for eligible patients. Health experts believe easier access may encourage more women to seek professional advice sooner rather than delaying treatment because of appointment availability or cost concerns. Looking Ahead The early success of the NHS pharmacy initiative suggests that community pharmacies will continue playing a central role in delivering reproductive healthcare services across England. With hundreds of thousands of consultations already completed, the program demonstrates strong demand for accessible healthcare delivered closer to home. As pharmacies continue expanding clinical services, patients may benefit from quicker treatment, improved convenience, and reduced pressure on other parts of the NHS. Emergency contraception remains an important option for women who experience contraceptive failure or unprotected sex. The availability of free consultations and medication through participating pharmacies makes timely access significantly easier for many people across England. As healthcare continues to evolve, community pharmacies are increasingly becoming trusted first points of contact for many everyday health needs, helping deliver faster care while supporting the wider NHS. Always consult a qualified healthcare professional, pharmacist, GP, or sexual health provider for personalized advice regarding emergency contraception, reproductive health, or any medical concerns. Availability and eligibility for NHS services may vary based on local guidelines and individual circumstances.
